As per office report, notice has been served on respondent no. 2 yet no one appeared on his/her behalf.
Heard learned counsel for appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State-Respondent and perused the paper book.

This Criminal Appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed questioning the correctness of the order 22.4.2022 passed by Special Judge (SC/ST Act) Saharanpur (State vs. Aslam) arising out of Case Crime no. 62 of 2022, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, P.S. Fatehpur, District Saharanpur,
whereby his prayer for bail has been rejected.
Prosecution version in brief is that informant/ prosecutrix lodged FIR on 8.3.2022 at 18:50 hours stating therein that on same day, accused, who was her acquaintance, offered lift her on his motorcycle at around 7:00 PM and assured her to drop at her home, however, he took her towards some field and committed rape on her and threatened her with life, he insulted her by caste specific word.

It is contended by counsel for the appellant that medical examination of the victim was Aslam vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55004548/
1 conducted on 11.3.2022 by doctor, who had not recorded any internal or external injury on her person as victim has stated that accused had beaten on her chest, therefore, x-ray examination of her chest was done but no fracture was found therein.

sentences.text: He next submitted that accused is married person having grandchildren and victim is elder to him; prosecution version is not natural; accused appellant has been falsely implicated by the prosecutrix at the behest of some opponent of the accused.

He next submitted that DNA was taken of the victim and same was sent for examination but no sperm or semen was found on DNA sample and on clothes of victim; sperm was found on underwear of accused but accused being a married person, it is normal phenomena and same is not connected with the victim.

He lastly submitted that victim stated in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she was raped by the accused for thrice by force but no mark of injury was found on her person; accused appellant is in jail since 22.3.2022 for around one year, learned court below has rejected the bail application of the appellant without considering the material on record.
In medico legal examination report and in statement of the victim, her age is stated as 60 years.
Per contra learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and supported the impugned order.

He submitted that FIR of the incident was lodged at the instance of prosecutrix next day and prosecutrix has supported FIR version in her statement and made specific allegation against the accused for commission of rape against the appellant.
However he could not point out anything material on the contrary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of the victim and medical examination as well as FSL report and keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, the appeal has substance and it is, accordingly, allowed.
Impugned order dated 22.4.2022 is, hereby, set aside.

Let appellant, Aslam, be released on bail in aforesaid Case Crime on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i).
The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence, if the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;

(ii). The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(iii).

In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
